  1. 3−i
  2. −1+2i
  3. −2−4i

Tue, Sep 15th @ 2:46 PM|Elapsed: 0:15Incorrect

  • The complex number 3−i has the real part x=3 and the imaginary part y=−1. So, it corresponds to the point (3,−1), which lies in the fourth quadrant.

  • The complex number −1+2i has the real part x=−1 and the imaginary part y=2. So, it corresponds to the point (−1,2), which lies in the second quadrant.

  • The complex number −2−4i has the real part x=−2 and the imaginary part y=−4. So, it corresponds to the point (−2,−4), which lies in the third quadrant.

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only".
